blocks.text: תְּפִלָּה לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
uncertainties: This is the running header, set in square type with '44' at both corners. It is not a Rashi-script rubric and is not prayer text. I kept it only for page identification.

blocks.text: מִֽי־כָמֹ֨כָה֙ בָּֽאֵלִם֙ יְהֹוָ֔ה מִ֥י כָּמֹ֖כָה נֶאְדָּ֣ר בַּקֹּ֑דֶשׁ נוֹרָ֥א תְהִלֹּ֖ת עֹ֥שֵׂה פֶֽלֶא׃
uncertainties: This line is printed with full cantillation. It is Exod 15:11, but no citation is printed.
כָמֹ֨כָה֙: a '>'-shaped mark sits above the מ, which I read as qadma. Next to the final ה is pashta. The qadma reading is uncertain.
בָּֽאֵלִם֙: there is a small stroke under the ב. I read it as meteg, but it could be munach. The word is spelled defectively (no yod) as printed.
יְהֹוָ֔ה: I read zaqef qatan over the ו. The holam over the ה is faint.
כָּמֹ֖כָה: I read the mark under the מ as tipcha. Its exact host letter is uncertain.
נֶאְדָּ֣ר: I read munach under the ד.
בַּקֹּ֑דֶשׁ: the etnach is clear. The dagesh in the ק is small.
נוֹרָ֥א and עֹ֥שֵׂה: I read merkha, but these could be munach. The mark under the ע of עֹ֥שֵׂה is faint.
תְהִלֹּ֖ת: I see no dagesh in the ת. I read the mark under the ל as tipcha.

blocks.text: שִׁירָה חֲדָשָׁה שִׁבְּחוּ גְאוּלִים לְשִׁמְךָ עַל־שְׂפַת הַיָּם יַחַד כֻּלָּם הוֹדוּ וְהִמְלִיכוּ וְאָמְרוּ. יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד׃
uncertainties: שִׁבְּחוּ: the dot in the ב is small. I read it as dagesh.
לְעֹלָם is printed defectively (no vav). I kept it literally.
יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד is Exod 15:18. There is no printed citation and no cantillation.

blocks.text: צוּר יִשְׂרָאֵל קוּמָה בְּעֶזְרַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וּפְדֵה כִנְאֻמֶךָ יְהוּדָה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל. גֹּאֲלֵנוּ יְיָ צְבָאוֹת שְׁמוֹ קְדוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ גָּאַל יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
uncertainties: כִנְאֻמֶךָ: I can't tell whether the כ has a dagesh. I read it as having none.
גֹּאֲלֵנוּ: the dagesh in the ג is uncertain. The sentence alludes to Isa 47:4, with no printed citation.

blocks.text: אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וּפִי יַגִּיד תְּהִלָּתֶךָ׃
uncertainties: This line is centered in smaller square type, not Rashi script. It is Ps 51:17, with no printed citation.
The small type makes the vowels hard to read. I am unsure of the dagesh in the ג of יַגִּיד and in the first ת of תִּפְתָּח. Some marks could be cantillation; I see none for certain.

blocks.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים וְקֹנֵה הַכֹּל וְזוֹכֵר חַסְדֵי אָבוֹת וּמֵבִיא גוֹאֵל לִבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶם לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה׃
uncertainties: וְקֹנֵה is printed defectively, as ו-ק-נ-ה with holam on the ק. I kept it literally.
גוֹאֵל and בְנֵיהֶם: I see no dagesh in the ג or the ב. I am not certain.
גּוֹמֵל: I read a dagesh in the ג, but it is faint.

blocks.text: זָכְרֵנוּ לַחַיִּים. מֶלֶךְ חָפֵץ בַּחַיִּים. וְכָתְבֵנוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַחַיִּים. לְמַעַנְךָ אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים.
uncertainties: לְמַעַנְךָ: I read patah under the ע, shva under the נ and qamats in the final ך. This could also be read as לְמַעַנְךְ. Host letters are ע and ך.
זָכְרֵנוּ: I read the vowel under the ז as qamats (qatan), with no meteg visible.
I split this block off from avot_chatimah only for convenience. In print it is a single paragraph running from זָכְרֵנוּ to אַבְרָהָם׃.

blocks.text: מֶלֶךְ עוֹזֵר וּמוֹשִׁיעַ וּמָגֵן. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מָגֵן אַבְרָהָם׃
אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר לְעוֹלָם אֲדֹנָי מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים אַתָּה רַב לְהוֹשִׁיעַ.
uncertainties: The print uses plene לְעוֹלָם here, unlike the defective לְעֹלָם in Shirah. The line ends with a period.

blocks.text: מְכַלְכֵּל חַיִּים בְּחֶסֶד מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים בְּרַחֲמִים רַבִּים סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים וְרוֹפֵא חוֹלִים וּמַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים וּמְקַיֵּם אֱמוּנָתוֹ לִישֵׁנֵי עָפָר. מִי כָמוֹךָ בַּעַל גְּבוּרוֹת וּמִי דּוֹמֶה לָּךְ מֶלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה וּמַצְמִיחַ יְשׁוּעָה׃
uncertainties: There is a wide gap between סוֹמֵךְ and נוֹפְלִים. It is only spacing.
לָּךְ: I read a dagesh in the ל, but it is faint.
דּוֹמֶה: I read a dagesh in the ד.

blocks.text: מִי כָמוֹךָ אַב הָרַחֲמִים. זוֹכֵר יְצוּרָיו לַחַיִּים בְּרַחֲמִים.
וְנֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לְהַחֲיוֹת מֵתִים. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים׃
אַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ וְשִׁמְךָ קָדוֹשׁ וּקְדוֹשִׁים בְּכָל יוֹם יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה׃
uncertainties: סֶּלָה: there seems to be a dot inside the ס. If it is a dagesh, that is odd and should be kept literally (see notes). It may just be an ink speck.
The paragraph has no continuation on this page. The text goes on at the top of the next scan.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer for the New Year
uncertainties: This is the running header, with '44' at both corners. It is not prayer text.

blocks.text: מי־כמכה
uncertainties: The maqaf may be printed doubled (מי־־כמכה). This is a cue only.

blocks.text: Who is like Thee among the powers, O Lord, who is like Thee, glorified in holiness, awe-inspiring in fame, worker of wonders.
שירה
The redeemed sang a new song in praise of Thy Name at the edge of the sea, together they all gave thanks and paid homage and said: the Lord reigns for ever and ever.
צור

Rock of Israel, rise to the help of Israel and redeem according to Thine utterance Judah and Israel. Our Redeemer, the Lord of Hosts is His Name, the Holy One of Israel. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who has redeemed Israel.
Lord, open my lips and my mouth will tell of Thy fame.
uncertainties: This line is centered in smaller type, matching the Hebrew. There is no Hebrew cue and no citation.

blocks.text: ברוך

Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God and the God of our fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the great, mighty and awe-inspiring God, God the Most High, who performs acts of kindness and owns everything and remembers the good deeds of the fathers and will bring a redeemer for their children's children for His Name's sake in love.
זכרנו
Remember us for life, O King who delights in life, and inscribe us in the book of life for Thy sake, O living God.
uncertainties: I split this from avot_chatimah only to match the Hebrew keys. In print it is one paragraph.

blocks.text: O King, helper and saviour and shield, blessed art Thou, O Lord, the shield of Abraham.
אתה
Thou art for ever mighty, O Lord the reviver of the dead, Thou art great to save.
uncertainties: There is no comma after 'O Lord'. I kept it as printed.

blocks.text: מכלכל

Sustaining life with kindness, reviving the dead with great compassion, supporting the falling and healing the sick and releasing captives and keeping His faith with those who sleep in the dust. Who is like Thee, Master of might, and who resembles Thee, O King, who slays and revives and causes salvation to spring forth.
מי כמוך
Who is like Thee, Father of compassion, who remembers His creatures for life in compassion.
ונאמן
And Thou art faithful to revive the dead. Blessed art Thou, O Lord who revives the dead.
uncertainties: There is no comma after 'O Lord'. I kept it as printed.

blocks.text: אתה
Thou art holy and Thy Name is holy and holy ones praise Thee every day. Selah!
uncertainties: There is a wide space before 'Selah!', which I reduced to a single space. The paragraph has no continuation on this page.

notes: I read the full pages for s116 and s117 and all three enlarged bands for s116. I did not open the s117 bands because the full English page was clear at normal size. Where the bands overlapped, I took each line once.

Page continuation: s116 starts with מִֽי־כָמֹ֨כָה֙ (Exod 15:11), so it follows on from the end of the previous Hebrew scan. It ends with אַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ ... סֶּלָה׃ and the next part of the Amidah starts on the next scan. s117 runs parallel: it starts with the cue מי־כמכה and ends with 'Selah!'. Neither page reaches the reader's repetition.
Neither page has a Rashi-script rubric, a speaker siglum, a printed Biblical citation or a parenthetical Shabbat alternative, in either language.

Biblical material without a printed citation: Exod 15:11 (with cantillation), Exod 15:18 (יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ, with no cantillation), an allusion to Isa 47:4 (גֹּאֲלֵנוּ), and Ps 51:17 (the small centered line).

Correction candidate (Hebrew, s116, atah_kadosh): סֶּלָה seems to have a dagesh in the ס, where the usual form is סֶלָה. Check it at higher resolution. If it is real, keep it literally and record the correction separately.
Spelling that varies within the page (not corrections, kept as printed): לְעֹלָם (defective) in Shirah but לְעוֹלָם (plene) in Gevurot, and the defective וְקֹנֵה הַכֹּל in Avot.

Correction candidate (English, s117): there is no comma after 'O Lord' in 'O Lord the reviver of the dead' and in 'O Lord who revives the dead', while the other blessings have one. This may be the printed style; I kept it literally.
The Hebrew avot/zochrenu split is editorial and is mirrored in the English. In print, זכרנו through מגן אברהם is one paragraph in both languages.
